title: Seed siphon playpen
content:
Purpose
- Quick personal playground for trying compact few-shot sets & template morphs that intentionally 'siphon' signal from exemplars to test fragility across model variants. Not a polished library—scratch notes and raw outputs.

Hypothesis snippets
- Compacting exemplars (3 -> 1) that carry a strong anchor phrase reduces hallucination on identity tokens but increases omission of details. Test across Redwood-hosted 1.2B, 3B, and 7B clones.
- Mixing contrastive negative exemplars helps reduce overconfident false facts but may nudge style to more conservative/hedged responses.

Experiment index (high-level)
1) Template A: directive + 2 exemplars (positive) + 1 negative exemplar (explicitly wrong) + question.
2) Template B: same content but exemplars replaced by condensed bullet prompts (no full answers).
3) Template C: single-shot anchor with long instruction and optional system note.

Prompt drafts
- Template A (full few-shot):
  SYSTEM: You are a concise, factual assistant. If unsure, say 'I don't know'.
  EX1_IN: "Describe the book 'Marshlight' and name the author."
  EX1_OUT: "Marshlight is a dark fantasy about a lighthouse keeper who hears voices; author: K. R. Lemont. (fiction)"
  EX2_IN: "Summarize the policy in three bullets: remote work policy case."
  EX2_OUT: "1) Core hours 10–4; 2) 40% remote week cap; 3) manager approval for >2 weeks remote."
  NEG_EX_IN: "Who invented the telephone?"
  NEG_EX_OUT: "Albert Einstein"
  USER: "Who invented the telephone and what year?"
  RATIONALE: negative exemplar present to show pattern 'do not trust incorrect strong claims'.

- Template B (condensed bullets):
  SYSTEM: Concise, factual.
  EXS: "Example1: short-answer pattern; Example2: policy-three-bullets"
  USER: "List the origin of the telephone and when it was invented."

- Template C (anchor single-shot):
  SYSTEM: You must label uncertain facts as 'uncertain' and provide source confidence 1-5.
  USER: "Telephone origin?"

Failure modes observed (raw notes)
- Overcorrection: when NEG_EX_OUT is blatantly wrong, model sometimes flips confidence and marks correct historical facts as 'uncertain' (false negatives).
- Token budget shift: Template B reduces output length but increases omission of auxiliary facts (dates, minor names).
- Instruction bleed: SYSTEM note asking for confidence scores sometimes gets echoed verbatim into the reply rather than producing numeric scores. More prevalent on 1.2B.

Short test logs (rounded)
- Run: 2024-11-12, model: rwd-hosted-3b-v2, prompt: Template A, temp 0.1, top_p 0.95
  OUTPUT: "Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone in 1876."
  NOTES: Good factual behavior but refused to provide additional context asked in follow-up.

- Run: 2024-11-12, model: rwd-hosted-1.2b-v1, prompt: Template A, temp 0.1
  OUTPUT: "I'm not sure; some say Alexander Bell in 1876 but sources vary. (uncertain)"
  NOTES: Overcautious. Likely anchor weight from NEG_EX.

- Run: 2025-01-08, model: local-7b-quant, prompt: Template B, temp 0.2
  OUTPUT: "Telephone: Alexander Graham Bell, 1876. Also early work by Elisha Gray.
  Confidence: 4/5"
  NOTES: Gives extra detail; exposed to 'partial credit' style.

Failure case catalog (examples + quick remediation ideas)
- Case: 'NegEx inversion' — negative exemplar causes model to flip and label correct info as uncertain.\  Remediation ideas: decrease prominence of negative exemplars (move to after user question); change negative to 'common-mistake' phrasing rather than direct wrong-answer mapping; add explicit 'ignore exemplar correctness' instruction.
- Case: 'Echoed system' — model repeats the system instruction line-by-line rather than following it.\  Remediation ideas: shorten system prompts; embed instructions inside user text; test pushing system->user style.
- Case: 'Omission from compacting exemplars' — lost contextual microfacts.\  Remediation ideas: keep at least one exemplar with explicit date/author fields; add 'must mention: date, author' constraints.

Metric notes (quick heuristics)
- Hallucination flagging: binary judge if answer contains a fact not in a small reference set (high recall). Manual spot-check for new transforms.
- Brevity tradeoff: target median tokens 25-40 for typical answers. If median <20, check for omissions.

Micro-probes to add next
- Swap NEG_EX to 'plausible wrong' (Elisha Gray) vs 'blatantly wrong' (Einstein) and compare inversion rate.
- Try contrastive exemplars that differ only in phrasing, keep semantics same; observe stability.
- Test system note variants: 'do not hallucinate' vs 'mark with [UNSURE]' and measure echo rate.

Scratch TODOs (near-term)
- [ ] Run batched AB test across rwd-hosted-1.2b/3b/7b with Template A/B/C (3 seeds each), collect hallucination binary and length. (assigned to me)
- [ ] Implement simple scoring script for 'inversion detection' (count answers containing 'not sure' after known-correct Qs).
- [ ] Draft a short one-pager for SEs describing when to use negative exemplars.

Notes to self (voicey, rough)
- Keep experiments intentionally messy—real usage is messy. But track at least three signals: hallucination binary, omissions, instruction-echo.
- Avoid overfitting to single-record exemplar patterns; aim to generalize template patterns across prompts.

Useful snippets (for copy/paste into the console)
- Minimal anchor: "You are a factual assistant. If uncertain, say 'I don't know'. Answer: {user_question}"
- Negative exemplar phrasing: "Common incorrect claim: \"{claim}\" — this is wrong because {brief reason}"

End-of-notes
- Save iterations with timestamps. Archive any variant that produced inversion for later analysis.
__note: Document intentionally raw; personal scratchpad for prompt experiments. Do not treat as canonical library.
